One command builds a complete new snapshot, with no other manual steps.

criteria: Given valid credentials and no existing snapshots, when the user runs the build command, then a new snapshot holding every dataset in Data requirements exists when it finishes.

nodes.title: An interrupted build resumes without downloading again what it already has.

criteria: Given a build stopped halfway through the download, when the user runs it again the same day, then already downloaded stocks are not requested again and the finished snapshot equals one built without interruption.

nodes.title: Cleaning never changes a value without recording it.

criteria: Given a raw price the cleaning step corrects or removes, when the build finishes, then the health report lists that stock, date, field, value before, value after and the rule that made the change.

nodes.title: A build whose blocking checks fail is stored but marked failed.

criteria: Given a build where a blocking check (HLTH-02) fails, when it finishes, then the snapshot is listed with status "failed" and the loader refuses it unless the user asks for it by name.

nodes.title: The app shows a running build's progress live.

criteria: Given a build in progress, when the user has the app open, then it shows the current phase (download, clean, validate, cross-check, store), the share of stocks done and the elapsed time, updated at least every 2 seconds.

nodes.title: A build can be started from the app.

criteria: Given no build is running, when the user starts one in the app, then it runs exactly as the command does and its progress appears (BUILD-05).

nodes.title: A finished snapshot is never modified.

criteria: Given a finished snapshot, when later builds run, then every value in it is unchanged.

nodes.title: Rebuilding the derived data from a snapshot's saved raw data gives identical numbers.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when its returns, adjusted prices, universe and health report are rebuilt from its raw data, then every number equals the original exactly.

nodes.title: The same load from the same snapshot always returns the same result.

criteria: Given a load request naming a snapshot, when it is repeated after newer snapshots exist, then the result is identical value for value.

nodes.title: The user can list snapshots.

criteria: Given several snapshots, when the user lists them, then each shows its date, status (healthy or failed), date range covered, number of stocks and number of unexplained cross-check differences.

nodes.title: The user can compare two snapshots to see what the vendor revised.

criteria: Given two snapshots, when the user compares them, then every price, split, dividend and membership date that differs on dates both cover is listed with both values, plus counts per field.

nodes.title: The universe on a day is exactly the stocks that were index members that day.

criteria: Given a stock added to the index on 2015-03-20, when the universe is asked for 2015-03-19, then the stock is absent; for 2015-03-20, it is present.
Given a stock removed on 2012-06-01, when the universe is asked for 2010-01-04, then the stock is present.

nodes.title: The user's ten delisted former S&P 500 members all appear.

criteria: Given the user's list of 10 delisted former members, when a snapshot is built, then each has its index entry and exit dates and daily prices up to its last trading day, and the health report shows this check passing for all 10.

nodes.title: A stock keeps one identity through ticker changes.

criteria: Given a member that changed ticker, when its history is loaded, then prices before and after the change form one continuous series under one permanent identifier.

nodes.title: A reused ticker never merges two companies.

criteria: Given a ticker held by one company until 2008 and by another from 2012, when either is loaded, then each company's history is separate and neither includes the other's prices.

nodes.title: Daily member counts are checked.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when validated, then every trading day with fewer than 495 or more than 510 members is listed in the health report.

nodes.title: Split-adjusted prices are continuous across splits.

criteria: Given a 2-for-1 split effective day D, when split-adjusted closes are loaded, then the raw close before D is divided by 2 and the day-D return reflects only the market move.

nodes.title: Daily price return is the change in split-adjusted close.

criteria: Given split-adjusted closes 100 then 102, when the price return is loaded, then it is 0.02.

nodes.title: Daily total return adds the cash dividend on its ex-date.

criteria: Given a close of 100, a $1 dividend with ex-date the next day and a next-day close of 100, when the total return is loaded, then it is 0.01 for the ex-date.

nodes.title: Adjustments come from the snapshot's own recorded corporate actions.

criteria: Given a split or dividend corrected by cleaning (BUILD-03), when the snapshot is built, then adjusted prices and returns use the corrected value.

nodes.title: No values are invented after a stock's last trading day.

criteria: Given a stock delisted on day D, when its data is loaded for a range past D, then rows end at D with no filled-forward prices or returns.

nodes.title: The report lists every check run, not only failures.

criteria: Given a build, when its report is opened, then every check appears with its result, its severity (blocking or warning) and the number of records affected, including checks with zero.

nodes.title: The build runs at least these checks: missing trading days for a member, non-positive prices, high below low, close outside the day's high–low range, duplicate dates, daily moves beyond ±50% with no corporate action, splits with no matching price move, member days with no price, daily member counts (UNIV-05) and the ten-delisted check (UNIV-02).

criteria: Given a snapshot seeded with one example of each problem, when validated, then each check reports exactly that example.

nodes.title: Surviving stocks' closes are cross-checked against the second source.

criteria: Given a surviving stock, when cross-checked, then every day its split-adjusted close differs from the second source by more than 0.5% is listed with both values.

nodes.title: Splits are cross-checked against the second source.

criteria: Given a surviving stock, when cross-checked, then every split that is missing from either source, or differs in ratio or date, is listed.

nodes.title: Dividends are cross-checked against the second source.

criteria: Given a surviving stock, when cross-checked, then every dividend missing from either source, or differing by more than $0.01 or in ex-date, is listed.

nodes.title: Stocks the second source cannot check are counted, not skipped silently.

criteria: Given delisted members, when cross-checked, then the report shows them as "not cross-checkable" with their count.

nodes.title: The user can attach an explanation to a difference.

criteria: Given a listed difference, when the user records an explanation, then the difference shows as explained with that note, and the snapshot's unexplained count drops by one.

nodes.title: Explanations carry to later snapshots.

criteria: Given an explained difference, when a later snapshot finds the same difference (same stock, date, field and values), then it is shown as explained with the same note.

nodes.title: One call returns any slice.

criteria: Given stocks, a date range and fields, when the user makes one loader call, then it returns a table with one row per stock per trading day and one column per field.

nodes.title: The loader offers raw open, high, low, close and volume, split-adjusted prices, price return, total return, and dividend and split amounts.

criteria: Given a request for each field, when loaded, then each column matches its definition in PRICE.

nodes.title: Asking for the universe returns each stock only on its member days.

criteria: Given a request for the point-in-time universe over 2008–2010, when loaded, then a stock removed in 2009 has rows only up to its exit date.

nodes.title: Without a named snapshot, the loader uses the latest healthy one.

criteria: Given a healthy snapshot and a newer failed one, when the user loads without naming one, then the healthy one is used.

nodes.title: Every result says which snapshot it came from.

criteria: Given any load, when it returns, then the result carries the snapshot's name.

nodes.title: The dataset is characterised with the data-analysis skill, given a snapshot's point-in-time universe returns and coverage; it passes when the report shows coverage and missingness by year, the cross-sectional distribution of daily returns with its tails, the largest moves with their dates, and the member count over time, each with its plot.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when the analysis is run, then the report contains each listed item with a plot.

nodes.title: The analysis shows the size of survivorship bias.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when the analysis is run, then it plots the equal-weighted total return of the point-in-time universe against the same for only today's members, over the full history, with the annualised difference.

nodes.title: Rerunning the analysis on the same snapshot gives the same numbers.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when the analysis runs twice, then every number in both reports is identical.

nodes.title: Every view shows data from the chosen snapshot, named on screen.

criteria: Given two snapshots, when the user switches between them, then all views reload from the chosen one and its name and status stay visible.

nodes.title: A stock view charts its full price history with its events.

criteria: Given any member, when opened, then raw and split-adjusted closes are charted with splits, dividends and index entry and exit marked on their dates.

nodes.title: A universe view shows the members on any day.

criteria: Given a date, when chosen, then the members and their count are shown, and stepping to the next trading day highlights who joined and who left.

nodes.title: A health view lists the report's findings, filterable.

criteria: Given a snapshot's report, when opened, then findings can be filtered by check, stock, severity and explained or unexplained.

nodes.title: A finding opens the stock view at its date.

criteria: Given a finding for stock S on day D, when the user selects it, then the stock view opens for S centred on D.

nodes.title: A cross-check view overlays both sources for a surviving stock.

criteria: Given a surviving stock, when opened, then both sources' split-adjusted closes are drawn together and days beyond the 0.5% tolerance are highlighted.

nodes.title: The user records difference explanations in the app.

criteria: Given an unexplained difference, when the user writes a note in the health view, then it is saved as in HLTH-07.

nodes.title: The interface is designed with the frontend-design skill to a deliberate visual direction, not a default dashboard; it passes when the user approves that direction from mock-ups of the stock and health views before the views are built.

criteria: Given the mock-ups, when the user reviews them, then the user approves the direction or the views are not built.

nodes.title: Daily open, high, low, close and volume for every stock that was an S&P 500 member at any time in the covered history, including those since delisted, from the earliest date the primary source provides.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when coverage is checked, then every stock in the membership history has prices for every trading day of its membership on or after the first covered day.

nodes.title: S&P 500 membership history: each member's entry and exit dates, including members since delisted.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when membership is read, then every member has an entry date and, if it left, an exit date.

nodes.title: Splits with effective date and ratio, and cash dividends with ex-date and amount, for every member.

criteria: Given a member that split or paid a dividend, when its corporate actions are read, then each event appears with its date and value.

nodes.title: A permanent identifier per company, with its ticker history.

criteria: Given a company that changed ticker, when its record is read, then it has one identifier and each ticker with the dates it held it.

nodes.title: For surviving members: daily closes, splits and dividends from a second, independent source, used only for cross-checking.

criteria: Given a surviving member, when the cross-check data is read, then it holds that stock's closes, splits and dividends over the dates the second source provides.

nodes.title: US exchange trading days only.

criteria: Given a weekend or market holiday, when any data is loaded for it, then no row exists for that day.

nodes.title: Data costs stay at or under $50 a month in total.

criteria: Checked against the monthly subscription charges of every data source used.

nodes.title: Everything runs on the user's MacBook Pro (Apple Silicon) with no remote servers.

criteria: Checked by running a full build, a load and the app with no services other than the data sources.

nodes.title: A full build from scratch finishes in ≤ 2 hours; a refresh that reuses unchanged history in ≤ 15 minutes.

criteria: Timed on the user's machine.

nodes.title: Loading one year of daily closes for the whole point-in-time universe takes ≤ 2 seconds; the full history, ≤ 15 seconds.

criteria: Timed on the user's machine after the snapshot is first opened.

nodes.title: In the app, a stock's full-history chart appears ≤ 1 second after it is selected.

criteria: Timed on the user's machine.

nodes.title: The app accepts connections only from the same machine.

criteria: Checked by trying to open it from another device on the same network: the connection is refused.

nodes.title: Credentials never appear in full in logs, reports, progress messages or the app.

criteria: Checked by searching every output of a build for the credential values.

nodes.title: One snapshot takes ≤ 5 GB of disk.

criteria: Measured on the first full build.

criteria: Given the user's list of 10 delisted former members, when a snapshot is built, then each has its index entry and exit dates and daily prices up to its last trading day, and the health report shows this check passing for all 10.

nodes.title: A stock keeps one identity through ticker changes.

criteria: Given a member that changed ticker, when its history is loaded, then prices before and after the change form one continuous series under one permanent identifier.

nodes.title: A reused ticker never merges two companies.

criteria: Given a ticker held by one company until 2008 and by another from 2012, when either is loaded, then each company's history is separate and neither includes the other's prices.

nodes.title: Daily member counts are checked.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when validated, then every trading day with fewer than 495 or more than 510 members is listed in the health report.

nodes.title: Split-adjusted prices are continuous across splits.

criteria: Given a 2-for-1 split effective day D, when split-adjusted closes are loaded, then the raw close before D is divided by 2 and the day-D return reflects only the market move.

nodes.title: Daily price return is the change in split-adjusted close.

criteria: Given split-adjusted closes 100 then 102, when the price return is loaded, then it is 0.02.

nodes.title: Daily total return adds the cash dividend on its ex-date.

criteria: Given a close of 100, a $1 dividend with ex-date the next day and a next-day close of 100, when the total return is loaded, then it is 0.01 for the ex-date.

nodes.title: Adjustments come from the snapshot's own recorded corporate actions.

criteria: Given a split or dividend corrected by cleaning (BUILD-03), when the snapshot is built, then adjusted prices and returns use the corrected value.

nodes.title: No values are invented after a stock's last trading day.

criteria: Given a stock delisted on day D, when its data is loaded for a range past D, then rows end at D with no filled-forward prices or returns.

nodes.title: The report lists every check run, not only failures.

criteria: Given a build, when its report is opened, then every check appears with its result, its severity (blocking or warning) and the number of records affected, including checks with zero.

nodes.title: The build runs at least these checks: missing trading days for a member, non-positive prices, high below low, close outside the day's high–low range, duplicate dates, daily moves beyond ±50% with no corporate action, splits with no matching price move, member days with no price, daily member counts (UNIV-05) and the ten-delisted check (UNIV-02).

criteria: Given a snapshot seeded with one example of each problem, when validated, then each check reports exactly that example.

nodes.title: Surviving stocks' closes are cross-checked against the second source.

criteria: Given a surviving stock, when cross-checked, then every day its split-adjusted close differs from the second source by more than 0.5% is listed with both values.

nodes.title: Splits are cross-checked against the second source.

criteria: Given a surviving stock, when cross-checked, then every split that is missing from either source, or differs in ratio or date, is listed.

nodes.title: Dividends are cross-checked against the second source.

criteria: Given a surviving stock, when cross-checked, then every dividend missing from either source, or differing by more than $0.01 or in ex-date, is listed.

nodes.title: Stocks the second source cannot check are counted, not skipped silently.

criteria: Given delisted members, when cross-checked, then the report shows them as "not cross-checkable" with their count.

nodes.title: The user can attach an explanation to a difference.

criteria: Given a listed difference, when the user records an explanation, then the difference shows as explained with that note, and the snapshot's unexplained count drops by one.

nodes.title: Explanations carry to later snapshots.

criteria: Given an explained difference, when a later snapshot finds the same difference (same stock, date, field and values), then it is shown as explained with the same note.

nodes.title: One call returns any slice.

criteria: Given stocks, a date range and fields, when the user makes one loader call, then it returns a table with one row per stock per trading day and one column per field.

nodes.title: The loader offers raw open, high, low, close and volume, split-adjusted prices, price return, total return, and dividend and split amounts.

criteria: Given a request for each field, when loaded, then each column matches its definition in PRICE.

nodes.title: Asking for the universe returns each stock only on its member days.

criteria: Given a request for the point-in-time universe over 2008–2010, when loaded, then a stock removed in 2009 has rows only up to its exit date.

nodes.title: Without a named snapshot, the loader uses the latest healthy one.

criteria: Given a healthy snapshot and a newer failed one, when the user loads without naming one, then the healthy one is used.

nodes.title: Every result says which snapshot it came from.

criteria: Given any load, when it returns, then the result carries the snapshot's name.

nodes.title: The dataset is characterised with the data-analysis skill, given a snapshot's point-in-time universe returns and coverage; it passes when the report shows coverage and missingness by year, the cross-sectional distribution of daily returns with its tails, the largest moves with their dates, and the member count over time, each with its plot.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when the analysis is run, then the report contains each listed item with a plot.

nodes.title: The analysis shows the size of survivorship bias.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when the analysis is run, then it plots the equal-weighted total return of the point-in-time universe against the same for only today's members, over the full history, with the annualised difference.

nodes.title: Rerunning the analysis on the same snapshot gives the same numbers.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when the analysis runs twice, then every number in both reports is identical.

nodes.title: Every view shows data from the chosen snapshot, named on screen.

criteria: Given two snapshots, when the user switches between them, then all views reload from the chosen one and its name and status stay visible.

nodes.title: A stock view charts its full price history with its events.

criteria: Given any member, when opened, then raw and split-adjusted closes are charted with splits, dividends and index entry and exit marked on their dates.

nodes.title: A universe view shows the members on any day.

criteria: Given a date, when chosen, then the members and their count are shown, and stepping to the next trading day highlights who joined and who left.

nodes.title: A health view lists the report's findings, filterable.

criteria: Given a snapshot's report, when opened, then findings can be filtered by check, stock, severity and explained or unexplained.

nodes.title: A finding opens the stock view at its date.

criteria: Given a finding for stock S on day D, when the user selects it, then the stock view opens for S centred on D.

nodes.title: A cross-check view overlays both sources for a surviving stock.

criteria: Given a surviving stock, when opened, then both sources' split-adjusted closes are drawn together and days beyond the 0.5% tolerance are highlighted.

nodes.title: The user records difference explanations in the app.

criteria: Given an unexplained difference, when the user writes a note in the health view, then it is saved as in HLTH-07.

nodes.title: The interface is designed with the frontend-design skill to a deliberate visual direction, not a default dashboard; it passes when the user approves that direction from mock-ups of the stock and health views before the views are built.

criteria: Given the mock-ups, when the user reviews them, then the user approves the direction or the views are not built.

nodes.title: Daily open, high, low, close and volume for every stock that was an S&P 500 member at any time in the covered history, including those since delisted, from the earliest date the primary source provides.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when coverage is checked, then every stock in the membership history has prices for every trading day of its membership on or after the first covered day.

nodes.title: S&P 500 membership history: each member's entry and exit dates, including members since delisted.

criteria: Given a snapshot, when membership is read, then every member has an entry date and, if it left, an exit date.

nodes.title: Splits with effective date and ratio, and cash dividends with ex-date and amount, for every member.

criteria: Given a member that split or paid a dividend, when its corporate actions are read, then each event appears with its date and value.

nodes.title: A permanent identifier per company, with its ticker history.

criteria: Given a company that changed ticker, when its record is read, then it has one identifier and each ticker with the dates it held it.

nodes.title: For surviving members: daily closes, splits and dividends from a second, independent source, used only for cross-checking.

criteria: Given a surviving member, when the cross-check data is read, then it holds that stock's closes, splits and dividends over the dates the second source provides.

nodes.title: US exchange trading days only.

criteria: Given a weekend or market holiday, when any data is loaded for it, then no row exists for that day.

nodes.title: Data costs stay at or under $50 a month in total.

criteria: Checked against the monthly subscription charges of every data source used.

nodes.title: Everything runs on the user's MacBook Pro (Apple Silicon) with no remote servers.

criteria: Checked by running a full build, a load and the app with no services other than the data sources.

nodes.title: A full build from scratch finishes in ≤ 2 hours; a refresh that reuses unchanged history in ≤ 15 minutes.

criteria: Timed on the user's machine.

nodes.title: Loading one year of daily closes for the whole point-in-time universe takes ≤ 2 seconds; the full history, ≤ 15 seconds.

criteria: Timed on the user's machine after the snapshot is first opened.

nodes.title: In the app, a stock's full-history chart appears ≤ 1 second after it is selected.

criteria: Timed on the user's machine.

nodes.title: The app accepts connections only from the same machine.

criteria: Checked by trying to open it from another device on the same network: the connection is refused.

nodes.title: Credentials never appear in full in logs, reports, progress messages or the app.

criteria: Checked by searching every output of a build for the credential values.

nodes.title: One snapshot takes ≤ 5 GB of disk.

criteria: Measured on the first full build.
